South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 12/23/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Worsening shortness of breath and persistent cough with greenish sputum.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up two days after his last visit, during which he was admitted for exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and suspected pneumonia. He reports no significant improvement in his respiratory condition. Despite ongoing intravenous Levofloxacin and increased oral Prednisone, he continues to experience significant dyspnea at rest and with exertion. His cough remains productive of thick green sputum, and he notes an increase in the frequency of his nebulizer treatments to every hour due to inadequate symptom relief.
The patient describes persistent fevers averaging 101F and a notable increase in fatigue, which he attributes to both his respiratory distress and the ongoing infection. He expresses frustration and anxiety regarding his slow recovery and fears of potential complications.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + worsening fatigue, + persistent fevers, - weight loss, - chills, + night sweats. Pulmonary - + persistent productive cough with greenish sputum, + increased wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 130/76 mmHg - Heart Rate: 88 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 32 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 85% on supplemental oxygen (3 L via nasal cannula).
General: The patient appears significantly fatigued and remains in moderate respiratory distress, utilizing accessory muscles for breathing.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Severe wheezing on auscultation; decreased breath sounds bilaterally; prolonged expiration with prominent rhonchi; crackles audible throughout lung fields.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation with persistent bacterial pneumonia, as evidenced by continued respiratory symptoms, hypoxemia, and lack of clinical improvement despite treatment. 2. Persistent hypoxemia requiring increased supplemental oxygen; consider escalation of respiratory support if no improvement. 3. Increased risk for respiratory failure; potential need for intensive monitoring and intervention.
PLAN
1. Continue intravenous Levofloxacin 750 mg daily; consider adjustment based on culture sensitivities and clinical response. 2. Repeat chest CT scan to evaluate for pulmonary complications, including abscess formation or worsening pneumonia. 3. Increase supplemental oxygen to 4 L via nasal cannula to maintain saturation above 92%; consider non-invasive ventilation (NIV) if saturation continues to decline. 4. Increase oral Prednisone to 60 mg daily for enhanced anti-inflammatory effect; reassess in 48 hours. 5. Consult Infectious Disease for further evaluation and potential modification of antibiotic therapy based on clinical status and imaging results. 6. Initiate physical therapy consultation for respiratory rehabilitation and to improve functional status as tolerated. 7. Continue to monitor vital signs and respiratory status closely; prepare for potential transfer to the ICU if clinical deterioration occurs.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax remains hospitalized, with a focus on optimizing respiratory support and managing his COPD exacerbation and pneumonia. The treatment team will continue to closely monitor his clinical status, with an emphasis on timely interventions to prevent complications. He is encouraged to communicate any changes in symptoms or concerns regarding his treatment plan.
